extracted.intended_audience: German-speaking readers interested in public relations/propaganda (students, historians, PR practitioners, communications scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Archive/catalog page describing Edward Bernays' 1928 book Propaganda (German edition). Summarizes the book's themes and practical claims about public relations, distinction from advertising, use of psychological techniques, and its role for corporate and government communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, jargon-free language
rubrics_metrics.description: "In klarer Sprache, frei vom heute verbreiteten Branchenvokabular..." — the book is presented as written in clear language and free of contemporary industry jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favour prose that is plain and accessible rather than filled with present-day PR buzzwords; clarity of expression is presented as a quality marker for PR writing and explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish public relations from advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: "legt er in Propaganda dar, worin sich Public Relations von Werbung unterscheidet." — the work explains how public relations differs from advertising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing or evaluating PR work, explicitly identify and explain distinctions from advertising (aims, methods, scope), using arguments or examples to clarify the difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argue the necessity of steering mass opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Er begründet, warum es von elementarer Bedeutung ist, die Meinung der Massen zu steuern" — the book justifies why shaping public opinion is fundamentally important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include reasoned argumentation about the importance and objectives of influencing public opinion; a strong piece should explain why such influence matters in practice and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete examples to demonstrate methods
rubrics_metrics.description: "und erklärt einem ganz konkreten Beispielen, wie das geht." — Bernays uses concrete examples to show how influence is effected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide case studies or specific examples demonstrating tactics and their outcomes rather than only abstract theory; practical examples are treated as essential to persuasive PR writing or instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ psychological targeting (appeal to the unconscious)
rubrics_metrics.description: "wie sich über den gezielten Zugriff auf das Unbewusste Waren verkaufen oder gesellschaftlich unpopuläre Maßnahmen durchsetzen lassen." — discusses using targeted access to the unconscious to sell goods or implement unpopular measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge and describe psychological techniques (appeals to emotion, unconscious drives) used in messaging; candid discussion of such techniques is treated as a substantive component of PR practice and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide foundational principles for corporate and government communication
rubrics_metrics.description: "Er schafft damit bis heute gültige Grundlagen für Unternehmens - und Regierungskommunikation" — the book is presented as establishing enduring foundations for corporate and government communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present generalizable principles that can guide organizational (corporate/government) communication strategy; emphasize lasting frameworks, not only ephemeral tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalize change and progress through propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: "Propaganda gewöhnt die Öffentlichkeit den Wandel und den Fortschritt." — propaganda is described as a means to accustom the public to change and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing messages, consider framing that reduces resistance by normalizing change; evaluate whether communication successfully prepares audiences for transitions or innovations.
